title: Collection methods

blocks.heading: Collection methods
blocks.text: Questionnaires, interviews, observation and secondary-source research obtain different kinds of evidence. Specify who or what, where, when and how it is recorded. A bar chart presents collected data; it does not collect responses.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Questionnaires
blocks.text: A questionnaire uses a consistent set of questions with recordable answers. Use neutral wording, one issue per question, units and non-overlapping categories. Pilot it with relevant volunteers, protect privacy and allow refusal.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Interviews
blocks.text: An interview obtains information by asking participants questions and recording answers consistently. Explain purpose and consent, use a neutral schedule and ask clarifying questions without suggesting an answer. Interviews can explore reasons but require time and careful recording.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Observation
blocks.text: Observation records directly visible or measurable features through a planned record. Define categories, units, site and time before collecting. Count from a safe public place; do not handle waste or infer private motives from visible behaviour.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Secondary-source research
blocks.text: Secondary-source research selects and records relevant existing evidence. Note publisher, date, unit, population, method and limitations. A different district or old period may not answer the current local question.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Name and describe a way to collect fictional household water-journey times when selected adults freely consent. Use a questionnaire: explain purpose and privacy, ask return minutes including waiting for a stated recent journey, record the numerical response with date and non-identifying code, and allow refusal.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect the enquiry to its actual development topic and to Population (7.1) for denominators. Keep an individual record of the real procedure, changes, findings and limits. Fictional models teach the method and must not be presented as the learner’s completed fieldwork.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
